Maintenance Report — MNT-0007-002

Asset: WELL-0007 (SW-23 Well 007, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2023 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 30 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0007-0011 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 09 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0007-0011 at 08:00 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.6% of the pad area, estimated 0.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 336 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 269 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0007-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0007-009

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0007-0047 showed the wellhead at 28.3 °C with the air at 26.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.

  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Asset: WELL-0007 (SW-23 Well 007, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 11 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jan 2025 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 81 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0007-0113 on 2025-01-09 Report written: 16 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0007-0113 showed the wellhead at 16.4 °C with the air at 6.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0007-019

Asset: WELL-0007 (SW-23 Well 007, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 18 Apr 2025 08:00 · Finished: 13 May 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 596 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0007-0127 on 2025-04-17 Report written: 13 May 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0007-0127 showed the wellhead at 22.2 °C with the air at 22.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 23 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.
